findings.reason: the discriminator needs splitting into a key source (receipts only) and a relaunch test (any launch trace, marker included), and `s16` needs a two-door first-attempt case; without that the node closes `s13`'s window while appearing to tidy up.
findings.text: `s16` changes `run_holds_an_attempt_record` to read only worker/exit/`attempt-N` receipts, and that is the clause that catches a run's *first* attempt in flight: `dispatch.py:2772` writes the `attempt.json` marker 85 lines *before* the reservation block at `dispatch.py:2857`, so door B currently sees `attempt.json`, takes a reservation keyed off receipts (none) plus one, and is refused by door A's hold; with the clause gone the discriminator answers "never launched", the launch takes no reservation, and door B is admitted beside a door A still between its marker and its supervisor's `worker.json` — the exact window `s13` closed. `s16` justifies the removal by saying `s13` "declares `attempt.json` is no receipt", but `s13` excludes it from the reservation *key* so two racing doors derive the same key, not from the relaunch *decision*. `s16`'s done-when has no case for two doors racing on a run's first attempt, so its gate cannot see this.

findings.reason: without naming the naming owner, the node either adds a second naming path beside `_live_worker_naming` (the duplication `s8` and `s9` were written to remove) or fails its own (a1)/(a2) assertions, and a reader of the refusal would be told the worker is "an unrecorded process" or "placed on a scheduler job" when the run was launched on another machine.
findings.text: `s15` makes a foreign record's unknown reading "take the placed-unknown branch" of `_launch_refused_by` (`dispatch_launch.py:2151`, gated on `reading.arm == LIVENESS_PLACED`) and makes `_live_worker_refusal` "name its `launcher_host` and recorded pid", but a foreign reading is `LivenessReading(LIVENESS_UNKNOWN, None)` — arm `unknown`, no pid, no session (`recovery_liveness.py:1362`) — so the refusal's naming comes from `_live_worker_naming` (`dispatch_launch.py:2020`), which `s15` never mentions: it branches on the arm and would answer `"an unrecorded process"` for an unknown arm, or `"placed on a scheduler job, liveness unknown"` if the branch is reached by widening the arm test. `s15`'s done-when requires each of (a1)/(a2) to name the recorded `launcher_host` and pid, so as written the mechanism cannot produce the measure it asserts.

findings.reason: the base arm is the only control showing the guard is what turns (a1)/(a2) green, and as stated it can pass on a missing file, leaving the node's whole measure resting on an arm that never exercised the base code.
findings.text: `s15` writes a brand-new test file (`tests/test_a_worker_on_another_host_refuses_a_relaunch.py`, confirmed absent from the tree) and states only that "(a1) and (a2) fail at the dispatch base and pass at the head", while every sibling section says "with the new test copied into the base tree" (`s9`, `s10`, `s11`, `s12`, `s13`, `s16`). Run at the dispatch base without the copy, the arm exits non-zero because the path does not exist, so the declared control is satisfied by run and proves nothing about the guard.
